full_judgment:
3. The appellant contested the suit filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the property in suit is waqf property and Mutwalli is entitled to recover possession of the same. 

 6. Mr TH Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that in view of the provisions under section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 the suit against the orders dated 30-6-1986 and 11-6-1987 passed by the Administrator of Waqfs is barred by law and accordingly, the High Court Division erred in law in reversing the judgment and order of the trial Court rejecting the; plaint. The learned Counsel further submits that even on a plain reading of the plaint showing that the property is waqf property of Amir Ali Waqf Estate and that the appellant's title having been declared in Title Suit No.8 of 1934, the suit is barred under the provision of section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance and accordingly, the plaint is liable to be rejected. The learned Counsel further submitted that in view of the decree passed in Second Appeal No. 1192 of 1937 read with section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962, no suit could be instituted by any person against whom action has been taken under section 64 of the Ordinance by the Administrator and the remedy of the plaintiffs, if there be any, lay before the Waqf Administrator under section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance for a decision claiming title to the waqf property by adverse possession, inasmuch as claim of possession by way of eviction by Deputy Commissioner under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance is subject to an appeal under section 64(2) of the Ordinance before the District Judge. 

 8. The plaintiff-respondents instituted the suit for declaration of title by adverse possession and a consequential relief for a decree that the notices issued under section 64(1) of the Ordinance for eviction of the plaintiffs is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs on the averment, inter alia, that one Peer Box Sawdagar was the original owner of the suit land which was inherited by the predecessor of the plaintiffs Yakub Sawdagar by way of purchase on 24-2-1932 and have possessed mutating his name in the Sherista of the Zaminder and paying rent regularly and constructed a pucca building and planted trees, made pucca wall in the suit land. The father of the appellant-defendant No.1, however, instituted the suit for declaration that the property belonged to and was part of Amir Ali Waqf Estate and also for resovery of khas possession by evicting the present plaintiffs predecessor Yakub Sb. and grand-mother Fida Bibi therefrom. The suit being Title Suit No. 929 of 1931 was decreed on 22-8-1934 and an appeal therefrom being Title Appeal No. 375 of 1935 was dismissed on 19-8-1935. The second appeal being Second Appeal No. 1192 of 1937 was, however, dismissed on 27-7-1939 but the predecessor of the defendant never took possession by way of execution of the decree or otherwise evicting the plaintiffs predecessor and grandmother therefrom. The predecessor of the plaintiffs accordingly, continued in their possession in the suit land as before on payment of rent and after State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the suit land was recorded in the name of plaintiffs father without any objection from any quarter whatsoever and subsequently, the name was recorded in the PS Khatian and the father of the plaintiffs has been possessing on payment of rent and taxes to different authorities. Upon the death of the plaintiff's father in 1965 the plaintiffs as the heirs have been owning and possessing the suit land openly and adversely without any interference or interruption from any quarter and upon amicable arrangement between the plaintiffs and the deceased father, the plaintiff became the sole owner and being in possession mutated the same in his name in the record of right overruling the objections of the defendants upto appellate stage. The defendants. ultimately, took a short-cut measure issuing notices under section 64(1) of the Waqf Ordinance terming the plaintiffs as illegal occupants of the waqf property without serving any notice whatsoever and hence the suit. 

 9. The appellant though contesting the suit filing written statement but has, however, filed an application under Order VII rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the plaint on the ground that the said suit is barred under section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance and the plaint is liable to be rejected. 

 (d)  where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law: Provided that the time fixed by the Court for the correction of the valuation or supplying of the requisite stamp-paper shall not exceed twenty-one days. 

 10. Thus the plaint is liable to be rejected where it does not disclose a cause of action, while the relief claimed is undervalued, where the relief claimed for is not properly valued but the plaint is written upon an insufficient stamp paper and where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law. 

 11. The defendant has alleged that the suit from its own averment appears to be barred under section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance. While considering the application under Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court cannot take into account materials beyond the plaint to declare the case of the plaintiff as frivolous and vexatious and the Court is not required to take into consideration the defence set up by the defendant in his written statement or written objection. The question as to whether the plaint is liable to be rejected being barred by law must be apparent from the statement made in the plaint itself and not from the written statement or any other material other than that has been put in the plaint. Thus this provision applies when It appears from the statement in the plaint that suit is barred by any law either due to limitation, res-judicata or barred by law providing ouster of the jurisdiction of the Court. 

 15. In the instant facts of the case though the previous suit being Title Suit No. 990 of 1931 was for declaration that the property is waqf property and for recovery of khas possession which was decreed but no step was ever taken for recovery of possession by execution of the decree or otherwise and the plaintiffs and their predecessors continued in possession by mutating their names in the record of right on payment of rent and by construction of building and boundary wall allegedly, openly and adversely to the waqf estate or the Motwalli of the waqf estate since then and the plaintiffs have filed the suit challenging the order of eviction claiming title to the property by way of adverse possession.
